text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Politician Deri at heart of scandal over appointment of attorney general says lawyer who resigned is lying about affair.
- Prime Minister Netanyahu says neighbourhood for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem will be built.
- Defence Ministry says it has not been approached by U.S. on FBI investigation of classified information passed to Israel.
- Civil service to probe if Shas religious party deputy minister has too many advisers.
- Prime minister's cabinet secretary complains to right- wing legislator over his use of term loosely translated as 'Jew Boy' or 'Uncle Tom' in reference to U.S. ambassador to Israel.
- New owner may stop work of Africa Israel concerns on Jewish sabbath.
- Teledata Communications posted net income of $7 million for 1996 compared to net loss of $1.2 million in 1995.
HAARETZ
- Deri's defence lawyer to tell state prosecutor he wants Deri trial cancelled.
- American engineer admits passing information to Israel.
- Police renew investigation against internal security minister on alleged involvement in wiretapping.
- Compromise in surrogate mother battle between estranged husband and wife; man agrees procedure can go forward, woman agrees to divorce.

- Likud party central committee meeting put off 10 days due to rain expected on original date; newspaper questions how party can predict rain so far in advance when meteorologists can't, says Netanyahu wanted to avoid heat from hawks in party.
- Deficit continues to loom: 1.2 billion shekels in February after 1.3 billion shekels in January.
- Splitting Bank Hapoalim from Koor and Clal interests could still be condition for acquisition of bank.
GLOBES
- Netanyahu told police that Deri did not threaten him over appointment of attorney general.

- Parliament passes first reading of bill that would take sole power of setting key lending rate from Bank of Israel governor, placing power with committee of five including governor; Bank of Israel slams bill.
- U.S. fund management firm Franklin Resources of California announces it has reached 6 percent holdings in Scitex.
MAARIV
- 'Deri planned, acted to appoint Bar-On (attorney general)' Deri's former lawyer says.
- Agriculture minister defeats charges against him; his party now demands portfolio it first wanted - internal security.
- Contenders for Bank Hapoalim press prime minister's office to speed up tender.
- Bank Discount wins tender to implement grant of 1.8 billion shekels for set up of Intel plant in southern Israeli town of Kiryat Gat.
- Deputy director general of Africa Israel Shimon Harel announces he's leaving his post.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Police suspicions grow over attorney general affair.
- Rabbis investigated on allegations of providing speedy conversions.
- Former Shin Bet security service men now owners of security company questioned by police in connection with income tax allegations against Rupert Murdoch's News Datacom.
